body.p: A fox met a bear on a rock, at the edge of naked hills. The fox said to the bear: "Grandfather, let us lie down together." "Well, let's lie down", the bear said. "Lie down at the bottom." The bear lay down at the bottom, the fox at the top. The fox said sleeping: "Down, down, grandfather." The bear fell asleep. After the bear had fallen asleep, the fox pushed it down from the rock. Falling down the rock the bear broke its bones, it fell until it died. The fox went to the bear, it dried the bear. Having dried [it] (?), it made sausade out of [DCh]: The first clause is not really clear wrt. the bear's fat. The fox put the dried meat into the granary. Then the fox went off, it took along its sausage provisions its translation.(?). Going for a long time it met a human. The fox asked: "Where are you going?" "I am searching for food for me." "I have dried meat, let's go there", the fox said.[GVY:] DÊ¼ÉptilÉËlÉwi: an unclear form; probably a misprint instead of dÊ¼ÉptilÉËjÉwi (-jÉ- ACC.INDEF)? They went together, they went for a long time. Its friend was hungry, he couldn't go anymore. "Do we still go on?", he says. "It's quite close", the fox says, "you stay here, I'll go for it." The human stayed back. The fox went off, it went for its dried meat. Having gone not far away the fox started watching. The human was lying, he was lying, in an autumn night, hungry, he could not bare it, he froze to death. When he had died, the fox dried him as food for the winter.
